assign.request: UX rethink pass on /imagine/scenes/ — five sentences before/after, build and measure one real alternative layout, make it more visual, check persistence, land

log.msg: five sentences (before): what=a 3D lobby with five pedestals to click into; use=click a pedestal or its name below to step inside; goal=understand the four swap grains + observatory; hard=2/5 -- the doors read fine, mechanism jargon was already fixed by round 1; better=the fixed intro paragraph never updates as you go deeper, and at 3440 the doors cluster into the middle third of the canvas with dead floor on both sides -- an in-canvas dead-space bug distinct from the known column band

alternative layout built+measured: wrapped the foyer's intro+staging() in a .scene-lobby grid; past 100em it becomes rail(intro+door-switch) | stage(canvas) | notes(current door's readout), matching approved docs-three-region / the owner's 3-col-card brief; below 100em unchanged. KEPT: page-body height at 3440 went 987.6px -> 856.8px (13% shorter) with nothing removed; the real win is the current door's own note (e.g. WORLDS: Three arches...) now sits beside the canvas at any depth instead of below a 600-900px stage, off the first screen at every width tested. width-used/dead-space per the brief's DOM formula read 100%/~0px before and 100%/~50px after because this page opts out of the columns cap (width:full) so the outer body always saturates the metric -- not informative here, said so rather than hiding it.

in-canvas dead-space bug found+fixed: Stage.resize()'s vertical-fov widening only compensates NARROW screens (squeeze floors at 1 past aspect 1.6), so horizontal fov keeps growing with width alone at ultrawide and any fixed world-space layout shrinks toward the frame's centre. Measured on the foyer's 5-door colonnade: the doors' own visible span was ~33% of the 3440 frame before, ~63% after (portal() now reads the live stage aspect and widens `gap` past a 2.15 reference, floored at 1x so 1280-and-under never moves). Same fix applied to worlds/page.js's 3-arch crossroads (fixed radius 5.2 -> scaled the same way). Not applied to plinth/quarters/gallery/observatory, which show the same shrink to a lesser degree -- landing-page pass, technique documented in doc/decisions.md as a direct copy-paste for whoever does those next.

persistence: grep for store()|localStorage in public/imagine/scenes/ returns nothing -- this realm remembers nothing, no baseline() mark needed. Console: zero errors at 1280 and 3440 on the landing page and after navigating into worlds/dawn (checked after every edit). UI-test: clicked the Worlds door (post stem, hit-tested via the page's own hover tooltip first) at both 1280 and 3440 -- both navigated to /imagine/scenes/worlds/ with zero console errors.

assign.outcome: **Kept the lobby grid; the doors were the fix that mattered more than the numbers.** The foyer's intro + `staging()` now wrap in `.scene-lobby`, a 3-column card (rail | stage | readout) that fires past 100em — an alternative from the approved `docs three-region` shape and the owner's tonight brief, verbatim. Below 100em (1280 included) nothing changed. The real win: the active door's own note used to sit below a 600-900px canvas, off the first screen at any depth; now it is a persistent readout beside the room at every depth. Page-body height at 3440 dropped 987.6px to 856.8px (13% shorter), nothing removed. Also found and fixed a second, more interesting bug the brief's own DOM-rect metric cannot see: `Stage.resize()`'s fov-widening only compensates NARROW screens, so at 3440 the five doors clustered into the middle third of the canvas with dead floor on both sides — `portal()` now scales the colonnade's gap with the live stage aspect (same fix carried to `worlds/page.js`'s 3-arch crossroads); the doors' own visible span went from ~33% to ~63% of the frame. Zero console errors at 1280/3440, primary click gesture ui-tested at both. Persists nothing.
